sections.content: You know how to express conditions without *si* using *de* + infinitive or a gerund from B2 Unit 10. In professional memos, contracts and formal warnings, these compact structures sound brisk and authoritative: *De no ser así, aplicaremos una penalización* ('Otherwise / If that is not the case, we will apply a penalty'), *De producirse un fallo técnico, avisaremos de inmediato* ('Should a technical failure occur, we will notify you at once'), and *De haber actuado antes, habríamos evitado el recargo* ('Had we acted earlier, we would have avoided the surcharge'). A gerund also replaces a *si*-clause when both verbs share the same subject: *Revisando el anexo con tiempo, remediarías cualquier error sin problema*.

sections.title: Compact non-si conditionals
rows: Formal 'if that is not the case' (*De no ser así, habrá un recargo.*).
Real or hypothetical condition (*De surgir una urgencia, llámame.*).
Counterfactual past condition (*De haberlo revisado, lo habríamos remediado.*).
Same subject as main clause (*Actuando a tiempo, evitaríamos la penalización.*).

items.spanish: El informe debe enviarse hoy; de no ser así, el contrato prevé una penalización.
items.english: The report must be sent today; if not, the contract provides for a penalty.

items.spanish: De producirse un fallo técnico, tenemos tiempo de sobra para remediarlo.
items.english: Should a technical failure occur, we have plenty of time to put it right.

items.spanish: De haber detectado la urgencia antes, habríamos evitado el recargo.
items.english: Had we detected the emergency earlier, we would have avoided the surcharge.

items.spanish: Comprobando los datos antes del envío, evitaríamos cualquier problema.
items.english: By checking the data before dispatch, we would avoid any problem.

sections.content: After *de*, always use an **infinitive** (*De no ser así*, *De haberlo sabido*) — never a conjugated subjunctive (*De no sea así* and *De hubiera sabido* are both wrong). With a gerund condition, make sure the gerund shares the subject of the main verb.
